messages:
alex: FYI — evening GPU pool spiking after a customer batch. I'm oncall til 22:00; leaving notes for handoff.

oncall-bot: ALERT: pool 'stable-v2' utilization 83% (burst cap 90%)
```
20:41 atlas-batch started (50 jobs)
20:55 autoscale +2 nodes
21:04 queue depth 120
GPU%: 83
```
Dashboard: https://redwood.internal/dash/pool/stable-v2

maria: Can we throttle atlas-batch? Suggest reducing parallelism to 5 or move to low-priority queue.

devon: Reached out to infra contact and customer SRE. Asked customer to switch to `low-priority`. No response yet. I can hold past 22:00 if needed.

alex: If no reply by 21:30 plan B: evict jobs with label `non-critical`. Command:
```
rbctl evict --pool stable-v2 --label non-critical --dry-run
rbctl evict --pool stable-v2 --label non-critical
```
Also lowering per-job concurrency from 10->5 reduces token load ~40%.

jordan: I'll cover 22:00–00:00, can run evictions if needed. Quick check — burst credits remaining: 120
```
burst_credits.total=300
burst_credits.used=180
burst_credits.remaining=120
```

alex: Noted. Handoff doc updated (/handovers/2026-03-17-evening). Also tenants: atlas usage=156 (limit 200). If they keep going we may hit tenant quota before pool cap. Flagging for next-day review.

maria: ok, thx. ping me if you evict any jobs so I can notify product.

devon: will do. +1 to jordan covering. :thumbsup:

jordan: copied. I'll post end-of-shift summary at 23:55 with final metrics.

alex: thanks team — leaving phone on for quick replies.
